concept.name: MACD signal line
concept.definition: A 9-period EMA of the MACD line, plotted alongside it; crossovers of the MACD line through this signal line are the most common MACD trading signal.
concept.intuition: A moving average of the MACD itself, smoothing its turns so crossovers are easier to read.
concept.mechanics: Signal_t = EMA_9(MACD line). A bullish crossover occurs when the MACD line rises above the signal line, bearish when it falls below; because it trails the MACD line, it adds a further layer of lag.
concept.formula: Signal = EMA_9(MACD), where MACD = EMA_12(Close) - EMA_26(Close).
concept.failure_modes: Adds lag to an already lagging construction, and crossovers occurring at positive or negative extremes often mark exhaustion and reverse quickly.
concept.misconceptions: The 9-period setting is a convention, not an optimum, and the signal line has no meaning independently of the MACD line it smooths.
concept.example: If the MACD line is 2.0 and its 9-period EMA is 1.5, the MACD sits above its signal line — a post-crossover bullish state.
